shipped_rows.title_o: Delving into the detail: Greater episodic detail in narratives of a critical life event predicts an increase in adolescent depressive symptoms across one year
shipped_rows.authors_o: Salmon; Isler; Jose; Glynn; Mitchell; Dewhirst; Buxton; Gutenbrunner; Reese
shipped_rows.outcome_quote: We replicated the finding that greater episodic detail in the turning point concurrently predicted greater depressive symptoms, albeit with a modest effect size. Episodic detail did not depressive symptoms in the low or high point narrative, and nor did it predict anxiety symptoms. (...) In an older sample than Salmon et al. (2021) (emerging adults), we replicated the finding that greater episodic (internal) detail in adolescents’ narrative of a life turning point concurrently predicted higher depressive symptoms. (…) Although the current study does not directly test the proposed mechanism (self focus), it extends current research by ruling out the possibility that variability of episodic detail in any self-relevant narrative which solicits implications for self might predict depressive symptoms: the detail in neither the low nor the high point was significantly related to depressive symptoms.
